source_text:
Οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ γοῦν αὐτοῦ οὐκ εἰσὶν Ἑωσφόροι,

ἀλλ' «εἶδος Ἑωσφόρου·» μετασχηματίζεται γὰρ εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός. Προσποιεῖται
εἶναι οὐράνιος ἀστήρ· προσποιεῖται σύμβολον ἡμέρας. Ὡς λαμπάδες καιόμεναι.
Οἶμαι μὲν καὶ πάντας 12.1049 τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἀθέων δογμάτων εἰσηγητὰς εἶναι στόμα
τοῦ δράκοντος· εἴη δ' ἄν τι καὶ τροπικῶς νοούμενον παρὰ τοῦτο, ὅθεν οἱ λόγοι
ἀπολλύντες. Εἴποτε ἤκουσας λόγου προφάσει Χριστιανισμοῦ κατηγοροῦντος τοῦ
∆ημιουργοῦ, φέρε εἰπεῖν, πρεσβεύοντος τὰ Μαρκίωνος, τὰ Οὐαλεντίνου, τὰ
Βασιλείδου· ὅταν κακῶς λέγωσι τὸν Ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς, ὅταν τι ὅμοιον, ὄψει
ὅτι ἐκ στόματος τῶν τοιούτων ἐξέρχονται δαλοί. Τηρῶμεν οὖν ἑαυτοὺς, μήποτε
ἐκεῖναι λαμπάδες ἡμᾶς καύσωσι· μήποτε αἱ ἐσχάραι τοῦ πυρὸς ἡμῶν ἅψωνται.
Ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια. Οἷον πρόδρομός τις ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ καὶ δορυφέρει
αὐτὸν ἡ ἀπώλεια· ὅπου ἐὰν ἔρχηται, προτρέχει ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτοῦ, εἶθ' οὕτως αὐτὸς
εἰσέρχεται. Ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον παραδέξηταί τις τὴν ἀπώλειαν, οὐ παραδέχεται τὸν δράκοντα· ὅταν γὰρ ἁμάρτῃ τις, τότε, κνηθόμενος τὴν ἀκοὴν, διδασκάλους ζητεῖ
ἀπολούμενος· καὶ ζητῶν διδασκάλους, μετὰ τὸ ἀπολέσθαι εὑρίσκει τὸν δράκοντα,
καὶ παραδέχεται τοῦτον τοσούτων κακῶν πεπληρωμένον εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν.
ΚΕΦ. ΜΒʹ. Ἔδωκε δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ. Ὁ μὲν οὖν πάντα πειρασμὸν ὑποστὰς ἆθλα
λαμβάνει τῆς ὑπομονῆς αὐτοῦ πάντα διπλᾶ παρὰ τὰ πρότερον· ὁ δὲ Κύριος ἆθλα
δίδωσιν οὐχὶ διπλασίονα μόνον, ἀλλ' ἑκατονταπλασίονα· οὐκ ἂν δὲ διπλάσια τῶν
προτέρων ἔλαβεν, εἰ μὴ διπλασίονα τὴν ἀρετὴν ἐπεδείξατο.
thought_title: The dragon's eyes, mouth, and forerunner destruction
orientation: Origen is expounding the description of the dragon in Job 41, interpreting its eyes, mouth, and the destruction that runs before it as the deceptive work of Satan and heretical teachers.
pass_a_gloss: His eyes then are not morning stars, but 'appearance of a morning star'; for he transforms himself into an angel of light. He pretends to be a heavenly star; he pretends to be a symbol of day. Like burning torches. I think indeed that all the impious introducers of godless doctrines are the mouth of the dragon; and there would be something also understood figuratively besides this, from which the words destroy. If ever you heard a word under the pretext of Christianity accusing the Creator, let us say, advocating the things of Marcion, the things of Valentinus, the things of Basilides; whenever they speak evil of the Maker of heaven and earth, whenever anything similar, you will see that from the mouth of such people firebrands come out. Let us keep ourselves then, lest ever those torches burn us; lest ever the hearths of the fire touch us. Before him runs destruction. As some forerunner of his, destruction also serves as his bodyguard; wherever he may go, his destruction runs ahead, then in this way he himself enters. Unless someone first receives destruction, he does not receive the dragon; for whenever someone sins, then, having itching ears, he seeks teachers, being destroyed; and seeking teachers, after being destroyed he finds the dragon, and receives this one filled with so many evils into his own soul. Chapter 42. And the Lord gave double. The one then who endured every trial receives as prizes of his endurance all things double compared to before; and the Lord gives prizes not only double, but a hundredfold; and he would not have received double of the former things, if he had not displayed double the virtue.

choices.why: The dragon's eyes are not the morning star itself but only its appearance, emphasizing deception.

choices.english: for he transforms himself into an angel of light
choices.why: Echoes 2 Corinthians 11:14, where Satan disguises himself; 'transforms himself' captures the middle voice.
Uses the glossary term 'the dragon' for ὁ δράκων, keeping the biblical image.
The word means burning pieces of wood; 'firebrands' preserves the destructive, spreading-fire image.
Uses the glossary term for ἀπώλεια, keeping consistency with the work's vocabulary.
Uses the glossary term 'endurance' for ὑπομονή and 'prizes' for ἆθλα, fitting the athletic imagery.

pass_b_english: His eyes, then, are not morning stars, but "the appearance of a morning star" (Job 41:18), for he transforms himself into an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). He pretends to be a heavenly star; he pretends to be a sign of day. "Like burning lamps" (Job 41:19). I think that all the impious introducers of godless doctrines are the mouth of the dragon. But something may also be understood figuratively from this, from which destructive words come. If you have ever heard a word that, under the pretext of Christianity, accuses the Creator—say, one that advocates the doctrines of Marcion, of Valentinus, of Basilides—when they speak evil of the Maker of heaven and earth, when they say anything similar, you will see that firebrands come out of the mouth of such people. Let us guard ourselves, then, lest those lamps burn us; lest the hearths of fire touch us. "Destruction runs before him" (Job 41:22). Destruction is like a forerunner to him and serves as his bodyguard. Wherever he is about to come, his destruction runs ahead, and only then does he enter. If a person does not first welcome destruction, he does not welcome the dragon. For when someone sins, then, having itching ears, he seeks teachers, being destroyed; and seeking teachers, after being destroyed he finds the dragon and welcomes into his own soul the dragon, filled with so many evils.

Chapter 42. "And the Lord gave double" (Job 42:10). The one who has endured every trial receives as prizes of his endurance all things double compared to before. But the Lord gives prizes not only doubled, but a hundredfold. And he would not have received double of his former things if he had not displayed double the virtue.

problems.why: Not in text quoted; 'lamps' and 'firebrands' are, but 'hearths' introduces new image without basis.
problems.fix: Stick to 'lamps' or 'firebrands' from the verse.

edits.old: lest the hearths of fire touch us.

problems.quote: No spirit will pass through him
problems.why: Translation contradicts next sentence; should be 'nothing escapes him' or 'he misses nothing.'
problems.fix: 'No breath escapes his notice' or retranslate.

problems.quote: having itching ears, he seeks teachers while being destroyed
problems.why: Garbled syntax: the participial clauses do not connect clearly to the main action.
problems.fix: Restructure: 'because his ears itch, he seeks teachers; and having been destroyed, he finds the dragon'.

problems.why: Dragon, Satan, and devil are used interchangeably without explicit equation at each occurrence.
problems.fix: Note at first use: 'the dragon = Satan = the devil' and maintain consistency.

edits.old: having itching ears, he seeks teachers while being destroyed; and seeking teachers, after being destroyed he finds the dragon
edits.new: having itching ears, he seeks teachers, being destroyed; and seeking teachers, after being destroyed he finds the dragon

fixed: The reported problem about 'No spirit will pass through him' does not appear in the current English text; no edit needed.

The syntax of 'having itching ears, he seeks teachers while being destroyed' is awkward but does not misstate the source; the Greek uses a participle κνηθόμενος and a participle ἀπολούμενος, which the English renders as 'while being destroyed.' I have adjusted the punctuation to make the participial clause clearer without changing the meaning.
The glossary issue about 'the dragon' is a style note, not a mistranslation; the English consistently uses 'the dragon' as the glossary requires, and the equation with Satan is clear from context.

problems.why: In standard English numbering this clause is Job 41:22; 41:21 is breath and flame.
problems.ruling: Citation is wrong. "Ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια" matches English Job 41:22; the 41:21 verse is the breath kindling coals. The other refs (41:18, 41:19) use English numbering.

problems.source_quote: μήποτε αἱ ἐσχάραι τοῦ πυρὸς ἡμῶν ἅψωνται
problems.why: ἐσχάραι are hearths of fire, a different image from the δαλοί already called firebrands.
problems.fix: lest the hearths of fire touch us.
problems.ruling: "ἐσχάραι τοῦ πυρὸς" means hearths or grates of fire, not "δαλοί" (firebrands). The English merges two distinct images, so the lexical meaning is wrong.

edits.new: lest the hearths of fire touch us

fixed: wrong_scripture: Changed Job 41:21 to Job 41:22 to match standard English verse numbering for the clause 'Ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια'.
mistranslation: Restored 'hearths of fire' for ἐσχάραι τοῦ πυρὸς, distinguishing it from the earlier 'firebrands' (δαλοί).

problems.quote: welcomes him into his own soul, filled with so many evils.
problems.source_quote: παραδέχεται τοῦτον τοσούτων κακῶν πεπληρωμένον εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν
problems.why: πεπληρωμένον agrees with the dragon (masculine), not the soul. English makes the soul full of evils.
problems.fix: welcomes into his own soul the dragon, filled with so many evils.
problems.ruling: πεπληρωμένον is masculine accusative, agreeing with τοῦτον (the dragon), not feminine ψυχήν. The English 'soul, filled with so many evils' attaches it to the soul and changes who is full.

edits.old: welcomes him into his own soul, filled with so many evils.
edits.new: welcomes into his own soul the dragon, filled with so many evils.

fixed: Fixed misattribution of πεπληρωμένον: the dragon, not the soul, is filled with evils.

last_rejected.quote: when they speak evil of the Maker of heaven and earth, when they say anything similar
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅταν κακῶς λέγωσι τὸν Ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς, ὅταν τι ὅμοιον
last_rejected.why: 'when they say anything similar' renders ὅταν τι ὅμοιον, but 'they say' is added; the Greek has just 'when anything similar.' However, this is a natural English expansion. The sense is preserved.
last_rejected.ruling: ὅταν τι ὅμοιον: natural English supplies 'they say' from context; meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: having itching ears, he seeks teachers while being destroyed
last_rejected.source_quote: κνηθόμενος τὴν ἀκοὴν, διδασκάλους ζητεῖ ἀπολούμενος
last_rejected.why: 'while being destroyed' suggests concurrent destruction, but ἀπολούμενος is present participle of ἀπόλλυμι, 'being destroyed/ruined.' The sense is 'already on the path to destruction.' This captures the participial force adequately.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπολούμενος present participle of ἀπόλλυμι; 'while being destroyed' captures concurrent ruin adequately.

last_rejected.quote: he would not have received double of his former things if he had not displayed double the virtue
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἂν δὲ διπλάσια τῶν προτέρων ἔλαβεν, εἰ μὴ διπλασίονα τὴν ἀρετὴν ἐπεδείξατο
last_rejected.why: English uses 'would not have received' (contrafactual), matching οὐκ ἂν...ἔλαβεν...εἰ μὴ...ἐπεδείξατο (past contrafactual). Correct. 'displayed' for ἐπεδείξατο is fine.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐκ ἂν...ἔλαβεν εἰ μὴ...ἐπεδείξατο: past contrafactual correctly rendered; ἐπεδείξατο = displayed.
ἑκατονταπλασίονα = hundredfold; correct rendering, no issue.

last_rejected.why: This is marked as God's speech in the brief? No—checking voices: God is speaker in u02-open, u02-rem-early. This is u02-rem-close. The brief doesn't assign this section to God. The formula 'Chapter 42' introduces biblical quotation. The English doesn't attribute it to a speaker, which is fine since it's a section heading/quotation formula.
last_rejected.ruling: Ἔδωκε δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ: section heading with quotation; no speaker attribution needed.

last_rejected.why: 'δορυφέρει' means 'carries a spear for/protects as a bodyguard.' 'Serves as his bodyguard' is a natural rendering. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: δορυφέρει αὐτὸν: bodyguard/spear-bearer; 'serves as his bodyguard' is standard rendering.

last_rejected.quote: the Maker of heaven and earth
last_rejected.ruling: τὸν Ποιητὴν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς: Ποιητήν = Maker; standard rendering, correct.

last_rejected.why: 'Destruction runs before him'—checking if this matches LXX. The phrase 'Ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια' is quoted. The citation seems reasonable.
last_rejected.ruling: Ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ τρέχει ἀπώλεια: Job 41:21 LXX citation matches; reasonable.

last_rejected.why: 'And the Lord gave double'—Ἔδωκε δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ. This matches Job 42:10 in both Hebrew and LXX numbering. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Ἔδωκε δὲ ὁ Κύριος διπλᾶ: matches Job 42:10 LXX; correct citation.

last_rejected.why: 'transforms himself into an angel of light'—this is indeed 2 Corinthians 11:14. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός: 2 Corinthians 11:14; correct citation.

last_rejected.why: The Greek has 'ΚΕΦ. ΜΒʹ.' = 'Chapter 42.' The English renders this. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: ΚΕΦ. ΜΒʹ = Chapter 42; English renders it; no omission.

last_rejected.quote: But something may also be understood figuratively from this, from which destructive words come.
last_rejected.source_quote: εἴη δ' ἄν τι καὶ τροπικῶς νοούμενον παρὰ τοῦτο, ὅθεν οἱ λόγοι ἀπολλύντες.
last_rejected.why: παρὰ τοῦτο means besides this, not derived from this; the added figure is lost.
last_rejected.fix: But there may also be something understood figuratively besides this, from which come words that destroy.
last_rejected.ruling: παρὰ τοῦτο is loosely rendered 'from this', but the clause is elliptical and the figurative sense (τροπικῶς νοούμενον) and 'ὅθεν οἱ λόγοι ἀπολλύντες' survive; the reader is not materially misled.
